rust_fix: read_body refuses a JSON body that is not an object with 422 model_attributes_type at body, as the Python product does; before, serde accepted a JSON array for a struct, so PATCH [] answered 200. The generated validation test sends a positional array to POST and [], 1 and null to PATCH.
The v1 to v4 delete answers 204 with the application/json media type, as FastAPI's JSONResponse does in the Python product. The generated CRUD test checks the header and the empty body.
harness_notes: Every Rust product is the som_app package at its workspace root, so cargo gives all of them one fingerprint in a shared target directory and judges freshness by modification time. The harness removes the som_app units before each build, so a build never reuses another product's binary.
A product is ready only when its own process listens on its port (lsof), so a process of another run on the same port is never taken for it.

Products, migrations and cargo builds run as tracked process groups. SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT kill them all, refuse new ones, and wait for the workers before PostgreSQL stops and the scratch directory goes. A SIGTERM sent during a cargo build left no process and no directory.

code_review.reviewer: independent read-only review agent (no edits, no runs started)
fixed: 204 answers are now in the media type comparison. v1 to v4 Python keeps application/json on its empty 204 and v5 Python sends none, so the oracle expects that and the Rust v1 to v4 delete now answers 204 with application/json.

Interrupt cleanup: SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT handlers are set first in main; products, migrations and cargo builds run as tracked process groups; an interrupt refuses new processes, kills every group and waits for the workers before PostgreSQL stops and the scratch directory is removed; a failed PostgreSQL start is stopped. Checked by a SIGTERM during a build: nothing was left. The leaked scratch directories of two earlier interrupted runs were removed.
The generated validation test now sends a positional array to POST and [], 1 and null to PATCH, which the read_body fix is needed for.
The suite sends number, null and positional-array bodies and a JSON object as text/plain to POST and PATCH; the README claims now match the code.
The parity summary is complete only with one row per v1 to v4 case and lists the v5 cases under not_compared.
D1 strict checks add 1.0 for an int and 1 for a bool.
not_changed: A fault counts as caught by its category anywhere in the run, not on one named step (README, Known limits).
The timestamp rules are stricter than the normalization and also gate parity; both products follow them (README, Known limits).
Ports are probed and released before binding; a race fails a case and never passes it (README, Known limits).
